source.title: SplitMixer: Fat Trimmed From MLP-like Models

record.tranche_reason: Tests image-classification accuracy across SplitMixer architecture variants and datasets, including the effects of model size and architectural mixing choices. It does not test memorization of random labels or the training–test gap directly.
record.gate_note: Reported results bear on V3's convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison only indirectly: the study compares convolutional SplitMixer variants with ConvMixer and other cited models, but does not compare convolutional and fully connected models trained from scratch. No results test random-label memorization, widening past interpolation, optimizer generalization, batch-size generalization, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example removal. The paper notes that a fully connected spatial/channel mixing model did not converge, but this is not a fully connected versus convolutional test-error comparison. Results borrowed from other papers are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates accuracy–efficiency trade-offs among convolutional SplitMixer designs, without testing any listed version. Table 1's fully connected and MLP baselines are borrowed results. The authors' fully connected mixing experiment failed to converge, but supplies no held-out comparison establishing V3's generalization effect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that separable spatial convolutions and segmented channel mixing substantially reduce parameters and computation while retaining competitive accuracy, with an accuracy–efficiency trade-off and possible learning failures if models are reduced too far.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates a newly proposed convolution-based architecture using image classification accuracy and efficiency measures; it does not apply the original claim's random-label memorization or train–test-gap procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported accuracy changes with channel-mixing variant and segment count; ablations report effects of normalization, augmentation, gradient clipping, residual placement, and spatial/channel components.

fits_no_version.finding: SplitMixer channel segmentation reduces parameters and FLOPS, with accuracy depending on the variant and segment count.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Channel segmentation offers architecture-dependent accuracy–efficiency trade-offs in convolutional image classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing BatchNorm with LayerNorm or removing RandAugment lowers SplitMixer-I accuracy on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 in Table 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization and augmentation choices materially affect SplitMixer-I classification accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: The fully connected spatial/channel mixing configuration in Section 3.9 did not converge; no corresponding test accuracy or detailed configuration is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The attempted fully connected mixing configuration has an optimization failure, suggesting sensitivity to architectural inductive biases.

record.problems: The authors report no extensive hyperparameter tuning and state that some cross-model comparison results were borrowed from another study with different training duration and potentially different conditions. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying result rows: the study does not directly test any listed version. Results comparing SplitMixer variants and cited architecture results do not measure the behaviors specified by the versions.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold; neither the depth sweep nor channel segmentation establishes this threshold.
Held-out performance of convolutional versus fully connected networks trained from scratch; local connectivity's contribution; sparse connectivity and convolutional initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization and the effects of tuning or switching optimizers.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes that recover performance.
Dropout effects, including small-data regimes, underfitting, and joint removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps relative to other measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T3 classification and V3 tested_not_extracted designation. No qualifying rows or verdicts are warranted; cited architecture comparisons and the failed-convergence observation do not establish the specified generalization comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out natural-label performance.
Width sweep past the zero-training-error threshold and resulting test error.
The paper compares convolution-based architectures, but does not test convolutional versus fully connected classifiers trained from scratch or isolate local connectivity's effect.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Sharpness or other measured properties tracking the train–test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the test-accuracy effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
